You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The structure is described in the orthorhombic polar space group Fmm2, number 42, with Hall symbol F 2 -2, using fractional coordinates throughout. The supplied input cell is not the conventional F-centered cell: it has lattice parameters a = 10.90542878 Å, b = 10.89947163 Å, c = 4.17103771 Å, with interaxial angles α = 79.05231219°, β = 78.89167247°, and γ = 22.056015339999988°, and it contains eight atoms with the declared composition La₂As₄Au₂. To recover the standard setting from this input cell, the fractional coordinates transform as q_standard = P q_input + s, where the matrix P has first row (−0.5000000000000001, −6.650214604766707×10⁻¹⁷, −0.5), second row (−0.5000000000000001, −0.5000000000000001, 9.953161972528017×10⁻²⁰), and third row (−5.32720940700761×10⁻¹⁷, 0.49999999999999994, 0.5), and the origin shift s is (0.0, −5.551115123125782×10⁻¹⁷, −5.551115123125782×10⁻¹⁷), effectively zero. All coordinate values are rounded to six decimal places before any corrections; in this case the list of precision corrections is empty, so the stated positions already represent the real input geometry.

In the standard Fmm2 frame, the face-centered orthorhombic lattice hosts four independent crystallographic orbits, each of multiplicity eight, giving thirty-two atoms in the conventional cell. Lanthanum occupies the general-position orbit 8c with coordinate relation (0, y, z); its representative atom lies at (0, 0.118467, 0.007245), so the two free parameters are y = 0.11846699999999993 and z = 0.007245000000000168, and the remaining seven equivalents are generated by the F-centering translations and the mirror and twofold operations of the space group. Arsenic is split between two inequivalent eightfold orbits. The first, also 8c with relation (0, y, z), has its representative at (0, 0.161719, 0.507062), with independent parameters y = 0.16171899999999992 and z = 0.507062; these atoms lie on the mirror plane at x = 0, slightly offset in y from the lanthanum sheet and near the middle of the cell along z. The second arsenic orbit, 8d with relation (x, 0, z), places its representative at (0.2157555, 0, 0.2774705), with free parameters x = 0.21575549999999993 and z = 0.27747049999999995, so these atoms sit on the perpendicular mirror plane at y = 0. Gold occupies the more restricted 8b orbit with relation (1/4, 1/4, z); its representative is at (0.25, 0.25, 0.249873), where only z = 0.249873 is free while x and y are fixed at one quarter. Thus the gold sublattice forms columns along the polar c axis near the special line (1/4, 1/4, z), the lanthanum and first arsenic sublattices decorate the x = 0 mirror plane at heights near z ≈ 0.007 and z ≈ 0.507 respectively, and the second arsenic sublattice populates the y = 0 mirror plane near z ≈ 0.277, with the F-centering replicating each motif at (0, 0, 0), (0, 1/2, 1/2), (1/2, 0, 1/2), and (1/2, 1/2, 0) throughout the lattice.
